name: Model-based object tracking
definition: Recognising a known physical object from its 3D model, without markers or prepared images, and reporting its pose so content stays registered to it.
interop_reason: The object model arrives from another system (CAD), so its format and units must be readable by the tracker; the tracking itself stays on the device.

name: Remote (split) rendering
definition: Rendering a view on a server from the client's predicted pose and streaming the frames back for display, so a device shows content it could not draw itself.
interop_reason: Client and renderer are often different vendors; pose, timing and the frame stream must agree or the view lags and swims. Distinct from net.media, which carries video rather than a view driven by the client's head pose.

name: Live data binding
definition: Binding objects in a world to an external live data source (sensor, machine controller, building system) so their state follows the real asset, or the real controller drives the simulated one.
interop_reason: Every digital-twin use case stops without it: the twin and the asset are different systems, usually from different vendors (OPC UA, MQTT, MTConnect).

name: Activity and learning records
definition: A portable statement of what a person did in a world and with what result, readable by a system outside it (a learning record store, an employer, an assessor).
interop_reason: Training use cases finish without it but the result is stranded in one vendor's dashboard; xAPI and cmi5 exist and are rarely bound to world events.

name: Physiological signals as input
definition: Heart rate, skin conductance and similar body signals delivered to an application as a live stream, with the privacy constraints that go with them.
interop_reason: Sensors and experiences come from different vendors; without a shared signal description each adaptation is wired to one device.
